answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, released only after three unrelated confirmations, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Reaching the ledge of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The fable lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the orchard is where a second reviewer recomputes them.
